docs.text: Pick a script from the top bar. Each one has the same pages: an overview, installation, configuration, how players use it, and troubleshooting. Script What it does tr-crafting Crafting at benches, campfires and stoves, or anywhere, with a minigame, job rules and flexible prices. tr-mail Post offices, mailboxes, letters, packages, telegrams and mail carriers. tr-journal A physical journal players write in, with pages they can tear out and hand over. All of them are built on jo_libs . If something isn't covered here, ask in our Discord.
docs.title: Home

docs.text: Players walk up to a bench, a campfire or a stove, pick a recipe from a menu, and craft it with a short key-press minigame while their character works. Works on any framework jo_libs supports. A few extras (weapon names and stack limits) are read from VORP when it's installed. How it works ¶ Walking up to a crafting spot shows a prompt. Pressing it walks the player up to the bench (or turns them to face the campfire) and opens the menu: The first page lists the categories. If a location only has one category the player can use, the menu opens straight into it. Each category is a grid of recipes. A recipe shows what it needs, how much of each ingredient you have, and its stack limit. Recipes you can't make are greyed out. A recipe with several ways of paying has a Pay with slider (Q / E) instead. Picking a recipe starts crafting. You make one per round of the minigame, as many times as your ingredients allow. Failing a round or pressing Escape stops early, keeping whatever you already made. At the end you get a summary, and the menu updates to show what's left. Everything is checked again on the server before anything is crafted: the job and grade, the ingredients or money, and whether the result fits in the inventory. If it doesn't fit, everything paid is given back. Requirements ¶ jo_libs oxmysql A framework and inventory supported by jo_libs (VORP, RSG, RedEM:RP, ...)
docs.title: tr-crafting

docs.text: Put tr-crafting in your resources folder. Add it to server.cfg after its dependencies: cfg ensure oxmysql ensure jo_libs ensure vorp_inventory # or your framework's inventory ensure tr-crafting Set up your locations and recipes in the config (see Configuration ). Every item used in a recipe, both ingredients and outputs, must exist in your inventory's items list. Placeable campfire The placeable campfire uses an item called campfire by default. Add it to your items if you use it, or turn it off (see Props & field crafting ).

docs.text: General ¶ Setting What it does Config.Debug Extra logging, and the tr-crafting:testAnim command for trying animations. Config.KeyHashes Keys used for prompts. The first opens the crafting menu; the second puts out your campfire. Config.PromptDistance How close (in metres) you need to be to a spot to see the prompt. Config.PropDistance How close you need to be to a crafting prop (campfire, stove...). Config.AllowMovement Whether the player can move while the menu is open. Config.Minigame true for the key-press minigame (one round per item); false to craft once after Config.CraftTime seconds. Config.Webhook A Discord webhook for crafting logs (leave empty for none). Locations ¶ Config . CraftingLocations = { [ "carpenter" ] = { label = "Carpenter" , blip = "blip_mp_ugc" , -- leave out for no blip jobs = { -- leave out for anyone { name = "carpenter" }, -- any grade { name = "builder" , minGrade = 2 }, }, locations = { [ "strawberry" ] = vector3 ( - 1812.8 , - 426.44 , 159.95 ), [ "blackwater" ] = vector4 ( - 867.15 , - 1291.85 , 43.0 , 90.0 ), }, categories = { [ "Materials" ] = { jobs = { { name = "carpenter" , minGrade = 2 } }, -- optional: replaces the location's jobs here recipes = { [ "plank" ] = { output = { { item = "plank" } }, cost = { { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 } }, }, }, }, }, }, } locations are the spots players walk up to. Use a vector4 to make the player face a direction (the heading) when they start. jobs is a list: a player with any one of them can use it. minGrade and maxGrade are both inclusive, and either can be left out. A location can also have props (craft at any matching object) or a command (craft anywhere). See Props & field crafting . Categories with no recipes the player can see aren't shown. Animations ¶ Config.Animations lists the animations recipes can use. Each has a dict , a name , an optional flag (default 17, which loops), and optional props the player holds: [ "hammer_kneel" ] = { dict = "amb_work@world_human_hammer@kneel@male_a@trans" , name = "base_trans_base" , props = { { model = "p_hammerclaw01x" , pos = vector3 ( 0.1 , - 0.04 , 0.22 ), rot = vector3 ( 175.0 , 20.0 , 170.0 ) }, }, }, A prop's bone defaults to the right hand ( SKEL_R_Finger13 ). A prop can have its own props that go with it, like the plank and nails in hammer_table . Text ¶ Everything players read is in lang.lua .

docs.text: Fields ¶ Field What it does output What gets made: { { item = "plank", quantity = 2 } } . A recipe can make several things. quantity defaults to 1. Leave out for an action . cost What it costs: items, money, gold or rol, or a choice of those. See Prices . Leave out for a free recipe. costLabels Names for each way of paying, shown on the Pay with slider. jobs Who can see and make it, on top of the location's and category's jobs. See Jobs . limit The most of the output a player can hold. For an action , how many times it can be done at once. animation Which animation from Config.Animations to play. Defaults to craft . weapon true if the output is a weapon. label The name shown in the menu. Defaults to the item's name. image The image shown in the menu. Defaults to the item's image. onCraft A function run on the server after each successful craft: function(source) ... end . Prices ¶ cost takes anything jo_libs' pricing understands. Items: cost = { { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "nails" , quantity = 2 } }, Items and money together. Everything has to be paid: cost = { money = 1000 , { item = "earth_star" }, { item = "fire_rose" } }, Tools. An item with keep = true must be in the player's inventory, but isn't used up: cost = { { item = "iron" }, { item = "hammer" , keep = true } }, A choice of ways to pay. When the options are lists themselves, the player picks one with the Pay with slider in the menu (Q / E): cost = { { -- option 1 { item = "rock" , quantity = 10 }, { item = "wood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "coal" , quantity = 4 }, }, { -- option 2 { item = "hwood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "wood" , quantity = 5 }, { item = "porkfat" , quantity = 5 }, }, }, costLabels = { "Rocks & coal" , "Hardwood & pork fat" }, The slider starts on the option the player can best afford, and only the chosen option is charged. Choices of a single cost For alternatives that are each a single cost ($10 or 1 gold), wrap each in its own list: { { { money = 10 } }, { { gold = 1 } } } . A plain list of single costs, { { item = "a" }, { item = "b" } } , means pay all of them. Jobs ¶ Jobs can be set on the location, a category and a recipe: The location's jobs decide who gets the prompt at all. A category's jobs replace the location's for that category. A recipe's jobs are checked on top , for example a higher grade for one recipe. Players without one of them don't see the recipe. [ "Lockpick" ] = { jobs = { { name = "blacksmith" , minGrade = 2 } }, output = { { item = "lockpick" } }, cost = { { item = "iron" , quantity = 3 }, { item = "copper" , quantity = 2 } }, }, Actions ¶ A recipe with no output that runs an onCraft is an action : boiling a canteen, cleaning something. Give it a label , since there's no item to take its name from: [ "BoilCanteen" ] = { label = "Boil Canteen" , cost = { { item = "canteen" , keep = true } }, limit = 1 , -- once at a time onCraft = function ( source ) -- fill or clean the canteen here end , }, The summary uses the label: "You crafted 1x Boil Canteen." Weapons and stack limits ¶ jo_libs doesn't provide weapon names or stack limits, so: On VORP, weapon names and images come from vorp_inventory/config/weapons.lua , and stack limits from the items table. tr-crafting waits for vorp_inventory to start, and reloads them when it restarts. On other frameworks, weapons show a name made from their code ( WEAPON_FISHINGROD becomes "Fishingrod"), and there are no stack limits unless you set limit on the recipe. Weapons are given with VORP's own weapon function on VORP, and as normal items ( weapon_fishingrod ) elsewhere.

docs.text: Crafting at props ¶ A location can have props instead of (or as well as) fixed spots. The prompt then shows next to any matching object in the world, titled with that object's name: [ "campfire" ] = { label = "Campfire" , props = { -- [model] = prompt title [ "p_campfire05x" ] = "Campfire" , [ "p_stove04x" ] = "Stove" , }, categories = { ... }, }, The player turns to face the object instead of walking to a spot. Keep the list short: tr-crafting checks for each model near the player every half second. The placeable campfire ¶ Using the campfire item places a campfire in front of the player. Its model is a crafting prop like any other (add it to a location's props ), and whoever placed it gets a Put Out prompt. Config . PlaceableCampfire = { item = "campfire" , -- leave out to turn this off model = "p_campfire05x" , animation = "campfire" , -- while lighting it placeTime = 4000 , -- ms max = 1 , -- how many one player can have burning burnTime = 30 , -- minutes until it burns out (0 = until put out) -- jobs = { { name = "hunter" } }, } The item is taken before the fire is placed, so a campfire is never free. Field crafting ¶ A location with no spots can be opened anywhere, with a command : [ "field" ] = { label = "Crafting" , command = "crafting" , -- /crafting opens it categories = { ... }, }, Or from another script, on the client: exports [ "tr-crafting" ]: openCrafting ( "field" )
docs.title: Props & field crafting

docs.text: Other resources can add locations, spots, categories and recipes from their server scripts, in the same format as the config: local crafting = exports [ "tr-crafting" ] -- a recipe at an existing location (the category is created if needed) crafting : addRecipe ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" , { output = { { item = "chair" } }, cost = { { item = "plank" , quantity = 4 }, { item = "nails" , quantity = 8 } }, }) -- a whole location crafting : addLocation ( "blacksmith" , { label = "Blacksmith" , jobs = { { name = "blacksmith" } }, locations = { valentine = vector4 ( - 367.0 , 787.0 , 116.2 , 90.0 ) }, categories = { Metal = { recipes = { nails = { output = { { item = "nails" , quantity = 10 } }, cost = { { item = "iron" } } } } }, }, }) -- another spot for an existing location crafting : addPoint ( "carpenter" , "rhodes" , vector3 ( 1340.2 , - 1300.5 , 77.0 )) -- add to (or create) a category crafting : addCategory ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , { jobs = { { name = "carpenter" , minGrade = 2 } } }) -- remove a recipe, a category, or a whole location crafting : remove ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" ) crafting : remove ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" ) crafting : remove ( "blacksmith" ) Adding something that already exists replaces it. Each export returns true , or false with a warning in the server console. When the resource that added something stops, its additions are removed, and anything it replaced is put back. Registering on start ¶ Restarting tr-crafting reloads its config, so anything added by other scripts is lost. Add yours again whenever tr-crafting starts: local function register () exports [ "tr-crafting" ]: addRecipe ( "carpenter" , "Furniture" , "chair" , { ... }) end AddEventHandler ( "onResourceStart" , function ( resource ) if resource == "tr-crafting" then register () end end ) if GetResourceState ( "tr-crafting" ) == "started" then register () end Opening a menu ¶ On the client, exports["tr-crafting"]:openCrafting(key) opens a location's menu where the player is. It returns false if the location doesn't exist, the player doesn't have its job, or a menu is already open.

docs.text: A recipe offers "1 of 99" when it should allow fewer ¶ 99 is the cap for recipes whose costs never run out (only tools, or free). Stack limits should stop it sooner. Check that the item has a limit in VORP's items table, or set limit on the recipe. With Config.Debug = true , the server console shows how many stack limits were loaded on start. Item [nil] does not exist in DB ¶ A recipe with no output (an action) is fine. If you see this, check your recipes for ingredients or outputs written in the old VORP format, { name = "...", count = 1 } , instead of { item = "..." } . If it only appears when a particular item arrives in an inventory, another script is reacting to that item. A weapon shows a plain name, or no image ¶ Weapon names come from VORP's weapons config. On other frameworks, set label and image on the recipe. Recipes added by another script disappear ¶ They're lost when tr-crafting restarts. Register them on start: see For developers .
docs.title: Troubleshooting

docs.text: A post office system for RedM: rent mailboxes, send telegrams, letters and packages, and let a mail carrier job deliver the post between towns. Features ¶ Mailboxes : rent a numbered box (e.g. #0042 ) at any post office, name it, share keys with other players or a whole trade, and transfer or close it. Telegrams : written on a telegram form and delivered to the recipient's mailbox after a short delay. Players are notified when a telegram is waiting. Letters : post any note or letter you're carrying to another mailbox number. Packages : buy a box, pack items into it, and post it. Postage depends on weight. Notes : write a note at the counter, keep it, or post it straight away. Mailbox directory : a searchable public listing of registered mailboxes. Mail carrier job : carriers collect outgoing mail at the mail desk and deliver it to other post offices, and are paid by distance. Map blips show which post offices have mail waiting for you, and (for carriers) which have mail to deliver. Post office staff : a clerk at each counter, opening hours, and a camera that turns to the clerk while you're served. Discord webhooks log mailboxes being opened, renamed, transferred and deleted, keys changing hands, mail being sent and delivered, and packages being packed and opened. Requirements ¶ VORP Core and VORP Inventory oxmysql jo_libs (menus, prompts, notifications, inputs) MySQL or MariaDB. If you're on MariaDB 11.5 or newer , use the included tr-mail.sql as-is: it already contains a fix for that version's stricter text-comparison rules.
docs.title: tr-mail

docs.text: Database : import tr-mail.sql into your server's database. It creates three tables ( tr_mail_mailboxes , tr_mail_messages , tr_mail_access ) and the insert_mailbox procedure that hands out mailbox numbers. Items : add these items to your VORP inventory items table (names must match exactly): Item What it is telegram a received telegram (readable) letter a received letter (readable) mail_note a note written at the counter (readable, can be posted) box an empty box (use it to pack a package) package a packed package (use it to open) mail a letter being carried by a mail carrier parcel a package being carried by a mail carrier Give them whatever labels, weights and images suit your server. 3. Resource : put the tr-mail folder in your resources and add it to server.cfg after its requirements: cfg ensure oxmysql ensure vorp_core ensure vorp_inventory ensure jo_libs ensure tr-mail 4. Configure it (see below) and restart the server.
docs.title: Installation

docs.text: All settings are in config.lua , with comments explaining each one. The main ones: Setting What it controls Config.PostOffices each post office: name, clerk position and model, the counter, and the mail desk Config.Prices the cost of a first mailbox, extra mailboxes, telegrams, letters, notes and boxes Config.MaxMailboxes how many mailboxes a character can own or hold a personal key to (trade keys don't count) Config.Packages packages on/off, size bands (weight limit, price and name for each), maximum weight, and whether opening a package gives the empty box back Config.Directory the mailbox directory on/off, and results per page Config.RegisterDefault whether new mailboxes are listed in the directory automatically, or owners choose Config.TelegramTimer minutes between delivery rounds (how long telegrams take to arrive) Config.Job / Config.PaymentPerUnit the mail carrier job, and their pay per unit of distance delivered Config.AllowedLetters which inventory items can be posted as letters Opening hours, interaction key and distance, blip, camera, screen filter see the comments in config.lua Config.Webhook your Discord webhook for the logs Player-facing text (menus and notifications) is in the language file, so you can translate or reword it.
docs.title: Configuration

docs.text: Walk up to a post office counter during opening hours and press the prompt. The menu has: Telegrams ¶ All telegrams waiting in any mailbox you can open, from every post office. Select one to collect it as a telegram item, then use it from your inventory to read it. Mailboxes ¶ Your mailboxes at this post office , and the mail waiting in each. Select a letter or package to take it. Open New Mailbox rents a new box at this post office (the first one is cheaper). Manage Mailbox (owners only): Rename : the name shown in the directory. Add Access : give a key to a player by their server ID, with a private nickname that only you see in your key list. Remove Access : take a key back. Register / Unregister : list or hide the box in the public directory. Set Owner : hand the box to another player. You keep access if you still hold a key, through your trade or personally. Delete : close the box. Press twice to confirm; any mail inside is destroyed . Send Mail ¶ Send Telegram : write on the telegram form and enter the recipient's 4-digit mailbox number. Send Letter : pick a note or letter you're carrying and enter the mailbox number. Send Package : pick a packed package; the price depends on its weight. Buy Box sells an empty box. Mail to a mailbox at the same post office arrives straight away. Mail to another town waits for a mail carrier to take it there. Write Note ¶ Write a note on paper (costs a small fee). It goes into your inventory as a mail_note , and is immediately available under Send Letter . Mailbox Directory ¶ Search registered mailboxes by name or number. Select one to copy its number, ready to paste when sending. Packing a package ¶ Use an empty box from your inventory. A container opens: put the items in and close it. The box becomes a package with those items inside. Whoever receives it uses the package to unpack it.

docs.text: A writable journal for RedM. Players open a leather-bound journal, give it a title, and write page by page. Pages can be torn out to keep, give away, or pass as notes, and each torn page is its own readable item. Features ¶ A leather-bound journal with ruled cream pages and a handwritten font, opened from the inventory. A title at the top of the journal, which also becomes the journal's name in the inventory, so journals are easy to tell apart. Multiple pages , turned with Prev and Next , up to the number of pages a journal holds. Tear out a page to get it as a torn_page item. The page is only torn out if the player has room for it in their inventory, so nothing is ever lost. Torn pages open as a single sheet with a torn edge, readable by whoever holds them. A writing animation while the journal is open, and a reading animation with a sheet of paper in hand for torn pages. An optional screen filter while reading or writing. The journal and the torn page can be dragged around the screen. Saved automatically when the journal is closed. Requirements ¶ VORP Core and VORP Inventory oxmysql jo_libs , with the framework and notif modules

docs.text: Database: journals are stored in a tr_journals table. If your copy includes a .sql file, import it. Otherwise, create the table with: sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `tr_journals` ( `id` INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, `title` VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', `pages` LONGTEXT NOT NULL, `page_max` INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) ); 2. Items: add these items to your VORP inventory items table (names must match exactly): Item What it is journal_blank a new, empty journal journal_written a journal that has been written in (each one is its own journal) torn_page a page torn out of a journal (readable) Resource: put the tr-journal folder in your resources and add it to server.cfg after its requirements: cfg ensure oxmysql ensure vorp_core ensure vorp_inventory ensure jo_libs ensure tr-journal 4. Configure it (see below) and restart the server. To hand out journals, add journal_blank to a store, a crafting recipe, or a starter kit. Players never need to be given journal_written or torn_page directly; the script creates those.
docs.title: Installation

docs.text: The default settings are in config.lua . To change them, put your changes in overwriteConfig.lua , which is loaded after config.lua , so your settings survive script updates. For example: Config . MaxPages = 30 Config . UseFilter = false Setting Default What it controls Config.MaxPages 50 how many pages a new journal has Config.UseFilter true a screen filter while a journal or torn page is open Config.Filter "OJDominoBlur" which screen filter to use Config.Debug false extra logging in the server console

docs.text: Writing in a journal ¶ Use a journal_blank or journal_written from the inventory to open it. The mouse appears, and your character starts writing. Title: the line at the top. It's also the journal's name in the inventory (up to 30 characters). Writing: click the page and type. Tab indents. Prev / Next: turn the pages. Page 3 of 50 shows where you are, and how many pages the journal has. X (top right) or Esc: close the journal. It saves. While the journal is open, the game's controls are paused apart from push-to-talk, so you can type freely. The first time a blank journal is closed, it becomes a written journal ( journal_written ), named after its title. This needs room in the inventory for the written journal: if there's none, the journal stays blank and what was written isn't saved , so make room first. Tearing out a page ¶ Tear Page (top left) tears out the page you're on. It's greyed out on an empty page. If you have room, the page leaves the journal and goes into your inventory as a torn_page , and the journal closes and saves. If your inventory is full, you're told there's no room, and the journal is saved with the page still in it . Tearing out a journal's last page uses up the journal: it's removed from your inventory. Reading a torn page ¶ Use a torn_page to read it. Its inventory description shows the start of what's written on it. Close it with X or Esc . Good to know ¶ A journal belongs to the item, not the character: whoever holds that journal_written item can open and write in it, so journals can be given, traded, or found. Journals and the torn page can be dragged by any part that isn't text or a button.

docs.text: Nothing happens when using a journal: check the item names match exactly, that the tr_journals table exists, and that jo_libs starts before tr-journal . A blank journal doesn't turn into a written one (and the writing is lost): the player's inventory has no room for journal_written . No message when tearing a page with a full inventory: make sure notif is in the jo_libs { } list in tr-journal 's fxmanifest.lua .
